messages:
maria-support: AcmeCorp (tenant=acme_acmecorp_42) hitting 429s on their Dedicated pool since ~08:30. Calls to /v1/generate return 429 `rate_exceeded`. They switched plans last night. Can someone triage?

alex: On it. Can you paste a sample curl and a failing request id if available?

maria-support: sample curl below, response body: `{"error":"rate_exceeded","retry_after":30}`. Request id `req_20260317_acme_01`.

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -H "X-Tenant: acme_acmecorp_42"
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"hello"}'
```

alex: Repro'd from staging with tenant header -> 429. Checked serving logs: quota_selector returned `GLOBAL_FALLBACK` instead of tenant override. Relevant log excerpt: 

```
2026-03-17T08:27:12Z INFO quota_selector tenant=acme_acmecorp_42 -> tenant_quota=NONE, feature_flag(use_global_quota_fallback)=true -> applied_quota=global_default(60r/m)
2026-03-17T08:27:12Z WARN rate_limiter tenant=acme_acmecorp_42 request=... result=throttled
```

alex: Looks like the tenant-specific quota override wasn't picked up. I also checked pool autoscaler events — no scale-up happened because pool tagging didn't match the scale policy. Pool has expected tag `env:prod` but after plan migration tenant tag changed to `acme-prod` (weird). Autoscaler policy is `scale_on_tag: env:prod` so it ignored the pool.

priya: How did the plan migration change tenant tags? Was that part of the billing migration job?

maria-support: Yes, billing ops migrated plans and added `tenant_label=acme-prod` to the tenant metadata. They didn't add `env:prod`.

infra-nick: TL;DR: two failures stacking: (1) feature flag `use_global_quota_fallback` enabled for this deployment causes tenants without a matching quota entry to be assigned the global default; (2) autoscaler policy expects `env:prod` tag and thus didn't scale when the pool saw sustained queueing. Result: lower global_default quota + no scale = 429 storm.

sam: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) Flip `use_global_quota_fallback` -> false for the dedicated pool so quota selector attempts tenant override lookup without falling back to global default. 2) Reapply tenant override (quota units) for acme_acmecorp_42 explicitly. 3) Run a short warmup traffic job to trigger autoscaler once tags fixed or autoscaler policy relaxed.

infra-nick: I can flip the flag for the pool now. Doing it via feature-flag-service. Will post deployment id.

deploy-bot: feature-flag-service: toggle `use_global_quota_fallback=false` for pool_id=dedicated_pool_17 requested by infra-nick. change_id=ff-20260317-01.

infra-nick: Flag flipped. Change id ff-20260317-01. Confirming serving logs now show quota_lookup path (not fallback).

alex: After flip, re-run curl -> 200s for small requests. For larger runs we still need autoscaler to add capacity.

maria-support: I'll notify Acme that we've applied a fix and ask them to retry. Also opening a support ticket `SUP-2026-1034` and adding logs & repro steps.

priya: Longer-term items: (A) Ensure billing migration job preserves `env:prod` tag or autoscaler config supports tenant_label variations; (B) Add a health check alert for when quota_selector returns GLOBAL_FALLBACK for >1% of requests for a pool; (C) Add a guard: when feature flag enabled, don't silently ignore tenant overrides without an explicit audit entry.

sam: I'll own the autoscaler policy change (PR to allow alias tags and a short-term relax rule). infra-nick will own feature-flag audit patch. alex will verify quota reapply scripts. maria-support will handle customer comms.

maria-support: Thanks all. Customer acknowledged and will validate. I'll update ticket when they confirm. :thumbsup:
